statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n and, for every index i with 0 <= i < n, the entry r[i] is the least integer L such that 1 <= L <= n - i and the bitwise OR of nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[i+L-1] equals the bitwise OR of the whole suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1]. The bitwise OR of a one-element block is just that element.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Under these preconditions the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n, i.e., the answer has exactly one entry for every starting index of nums.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= r[i] <= n - i. In particular every answer is a non-empty subarray length and does not extend past the end of nums.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n, the bitwise OR of the contiguous block nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[i + r[i] - 1] is equal to the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n and every integer L with 1 <= L < r[i], the bitwise OR of nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[i+L-1] is not equal to the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n and every integer L with r[i] <= L <= n - i, the bitwise OR of nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[i+L-1] is equal to the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, r[n-1] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = 1 if and only if nums[i] is equal to the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, r[i] = n - i if and only if the bitwise OR of nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-2] is different from the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1 and nums[i] = 0, letting T be the bitwise OR of the suffix nums[i+1], nums[i+2], ..., nums[n-1], we have: if T = 0 then r[i] = 1, and if T != 0 then r[i] = r[i+1] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r of length n, for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, r[i] <= r[i+1] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000 for every k with 0 <= k < n.
